Much could be written of Tommy Green’s magnificent performances and those of Fred Rickards, Fred Bentley and others, but space does not permit.
Walker allowed Green to hand over with him at the end of the third stage, but Archie Bedford, Eddie Short and Bill Lucas saw to it that we maintained our unbeaten record for this race.

Carter, Footer, Penny, Herbert, Green, Scrimshaw, Lucas and Stimpson were no more endowed than some of our present men; they merely exploited their gifts more by plenty of hard training and by turning out regularly in all Club matches.
The race started promptly at 10.30 a.m. and by the time Westerham was reached it was apparent that the race rested between Ray and Green of Surrey W.C.

The race winner was International Fergus Murray (8:40) followed by internationals Herring and Green. Gerry North was 5th in 8:58 and Laurie O'Hara (still trying hard to duck under 9 mins) 7th in 9:03.4.
For purposes of comparison we have given calculated times for speeds varying from 5½ to 6¾ mph together with the actual times of the Green - Ludlow - H.Whitlock record holders of pre-war days.
At Crawley ( 30 Miles ) the position deteriorated as Surrey, led by the experienced Green began to gain places and a small group were fast closing on our leading man.

Behind Ernie were top rated British sprinters Green, Hoyte and Roberts plus Davies of Jamaica. These performances added to Carl Lawton's fourth place in the 10km walk back in March give Belgrave a highly creditable 2nd and four 4ths for 1977.
Back at Cwmbran on the Monday for the Cwmbran Classic Meet, Ernie was clear again with 10.71 from McMaster and Green, and in the longer sprint placed 4th with 21.73.
The "Junior" went to the powerful running of Walter Hesketh from Green of Reading and Jack Eastham of Bolton, team title going to East Cheshire Harriers.

Vern Blowfield went off on the long stage to Handcross and soon passed his man to put us in the lead once again. Len Marchant was our next but he lost the lead to Green of Reading. Eddie Short went off on the up-hill climb to Patcham.
